intro: 南锣鼓巷位于北京鼓楼与地安门之间，南北向，全长786米，宽约8米。所附资料称其与元大都同期形成，街巷两侧排列16条支巷，整体呈棋盘式里坊格局，并保存传统胡同与院落肌理。资料还记载，该巷旧称“罗锅巷”，1750年《全城全图》改称南锣鼓巷。现有材料同时描述其历史街区风貌与后来的商业、休闲活动。
1.intro_en: Nanluoguxiang is located between Beijing Drum Tower and Di’anmen, running north–south, with a total length of 786 meters and a width of approximately 8 meters. The accompanying materials state that it took shape during the same period as Dadu of the Yuan dynasty. Sixteen branch lanes line both sides of the street, which retains an overall checkerboard-style neighborhood layout as well as the traditional hutong and courtyard pattern. The materials also record that the lane was formerly called “Luoguoxiang” and was renamed Nanluoguxiang in the 1750 Complete Map of the City. The existing materials describe both the character of the historic district and its later commercial and leisure activities.

borrowed.zh:
整体与16条支巷有包含关系；胡同肌理保存不代表所有建筑均为元代原构。
“与元大都同期建成”“1267年”及“至今740多年”等表述并存，年代口径未统一；“唯一完整保存”等为来源原文判断，不能据此推定所有建筑均为元代原构。来源中的开放时间属于整体景区页面信息，未转用于内部节点。
borrowed.en: The overall area has an inclusion relationship with 16 lanes; preservation of the hutong layout does not mean that all buildings are original Yuan-dynasty structures. The statements “built contemporaneously with Yuan Dadu,” “1267,” and “more than 740 years to the present” coexist, and the dating standards are not consistent; “the only completely preserved” is a judgment in the source and cannot be used to infer that all buildings are original Yuan-dynasty structures. The opening hours in the source belong to the overall scenic-area page and have not been applied to internal nodes.

5.intro_en: Mao’er Hutong is located between the Drum Tower and Di’anmen in Beijing’s old city, running east–west, with a total length of 565 meters and a width of 7 meters. Materials from the Capital Window state that it was already called Mao’er Hutong during the Qianlong period of the Qing dynasty. The name has continued to the present; it was temporarily changed to Fourth Huihuang Street before being restored. Keyuan was formerly the residence and garden of Wenyu, while Courtyards Nos. 35 and 37 once belonged to Wanrong’s maternal family. Existing materials emphasize that the gates of these residences can only be viewed from outside and do not state that their interiors are regularly open.

17.intro_en: Ju’er Hutong is located east of Nanluoguxiang. The historical development of its name can be traced to “Juer Hutong” in the Ming dynasty; it was later called “Juer Hutong” with a different character, and the present name was established during the Xuantong period of the Qing dynasty. In 1990, Wu Liangyong led the renovation of dilapidated housing and addressed the traditional hutong residential environment through “organic renewal,” allowing it to retain the character of old Beijing courtyard residences while meeting modern residential needs. Public materials also record that the project received the Asian Architecture Gold Award in 1992 and the World Habitat Award in 1993. Ju’er Hutong remains a residential living space, and the materials do not state that courtyard interiors are generally open.

intro: 僧王府，即僧格林沁王府，是一处跨炒豆胡同、南锣鼓巷和板厂胡同的府址。北京市文物局公布的保护范围包括炒豆胡同75、77号院、南锣鼓巷110号南中、北院，以及板厂胡同30、32、34号院的现状围墙。另一份官方旧文称，王府规模较大，前门在炒豆胡同、后门在板厂胡同，并记载僧格林沁于1865年在山东曹州阵亡，其子承袭亲王爵后，民间又称此处为“伯王府”。
18.intro_en: The Prince Seng Residence, namely Prince Senggelinqin’s residence, is a princely compound extending across Chaodou Hutong, Nanluoguxiang, and Banchang Hutong. The protection area announced by the Beijing Municipal Cultural Heritage Bureau includes the existing enclosing walls of Courtyards Nos. 75 and 77 Chaodou Hutong, the south-central and north courtyards of No. 110 Nanluoguxiang, and Courtyards Nos. 30, 32, and 34 Banchang Hutong. Another official historical text states that the residence was large, with its front gate on Chaodou Hutong and rear gate on Banchang Hutong. It also records that Senggelinqin died in battle at Caozhou, Shandong, in 1865. After his son inherited the title of Prince, the site was also known popularly as the “Residence of Prince Bo.”

Public materials specifically state that today the main view is of the exterior of the residence and its gate, and this does not establish that the private courtyards or interiors are open to the public.

In 1955, under the care of Zhou Enlai, the state Ministry of Culture allocated funds to purchase it and made it available to Qi Baishi as a residence. Qi Baishi created a number of important works here in his later years. The memorial museum has been reconstructed according to his living and working conditions in his later years, presenting the courtyard environment and the artist’s residential and creative life. Mao Dun lived here from 1974 to 1981. The sitting room and reception room in the residence retain their original appearance, and materials including books, daily articles, clothing, stationery, and identification documents from his lifetime are displayed. Public information from the Beijing Municipal Government records that Mao Dun’s Former Residence was announced as a Beijing Municipal Protected Cultural Heritage Site on May 24, 1984. Another official historical text also states that the bedroom and study in the rear courtyard were arranged according to their original appearance during his lifetime.

24.intro_en: The former site of Chiang Kai-shek’s Beiping headquarters is the residence at No. 7 Houyuan’en Temple Hutong. An official historical text states that it was originally the residence of the Qing imperial clansman Zai Fu, with the building facing south and featuring a combination of Chinese and Western characteristics. After the victory of the War of Resistance, the materials record that the residence served as Chiang Kai-shek’s headquarters in Beiping from December 1945 to January 1949. During this period he visited Beiping to express concern for compatriots in the north, and in September 1948 dealt with the Liaoshen Campaign there. Another official historical text states that after 1948 the compound received a new occupant, the “Office of the Central Committee’s North China Bureau.” These are historical uses and do not indicate its current access status.

intro: 什刹海是西城区北部的开放性风景区，由前海、后海、西海组成，水面约34万平方米。官方史志资料记载，其历史名称曾包括白莲潭、积水潭和海子，并在元代经水利整治后成为元大都与京杭大运河相通的重要水域。文旅资料进一步将沿岸名胜古迹、民居纳入今日风景区范围，并称其为北京市首批历史文化保护区之一。
32.intro_en: Shichahai is an open scenic area in northern Xicheng District, consisting of Qianhai, Houhai, and Xihai, with a water surface of approximately 340,000 square meters. Official historical and gazetteer materials record that its historical names included Bailiantan, Jishuitan, and Haizi. After water-conservancy improvements during the Yuan dynasty, it became an important water area connecting Dadu of the Yuan dynasty with the Beijing–Hangzhou Grand Canal. Cultural-tourism materials further include the scenic spots, historic sites, and residences along its banks within the present-day scenic area and describe it as one of Beijing’s first historic and cultural conservation areas.

intro: 后海是什刹海后三海之一，与前海、西海共同构成什刹海水域。官方旧文记载，后海北岸、东岸曾是元代以来的重要城市活动区域；新中国成立后，水域及沿岸经历疏浚、护岸、绿地建设和环境整治。20世纪80年代整治后，后海结合环海绿地和新建景点，形成可供临水游览、垂钓、划船等活动的休憩区域。
34.intro_en: Houhai is one of the three rear seas of Shichahai and, together with Qianhai and Xihai, forms the waters of Shichahai. An official historical text records that the northern and eastern shores of Houhai were important areas of urban activity from the Yuan dynasty onward. After the founding of the People’s Republic of China, the waters and shores underwent dredging, embankment construction, green-space development, and environmental improvement. After renovation in the 1980s, Houhai, together with the surrounding green spaces and newly built attractions, became a recreational area for waterfront sightseeing, fishing, boating, and other activities.

35.intro_en: Xihai, also known as Jishuitan, is one of the three rear seas of Shichahai. Existing materials discuss it within the history of the Gaoliang River water system, the grain-transport system of Dadu of the Yuan dynasty, and the improvement of Shichahai. An official historical text records that after renovation, the island of Huitong Temple was restored in Xihai; the temple was concealed among rocks, pines, and cypresses, while a two-story box-shaped hall inside the artificial hill was used as a cultural salon, serving functions including sightseeing, cultural entertainment, and traditional local snacks.

36.intro_en: Yinding Bridge is a bridge along Shichahai and is associated with the “Yinding Mountain View” landscape corridor. Official reports state that from the bridge one can look west toward the Xishan peaks, with weeping willows and waterscapes visible nearby; “Yinding Mountain View” is listed as a strategic-level landscape corridor in the core area. The reports also state that lowering the height of the Jishuitan Hospital building restored the existing ridgeline view. Whether the mountains can be seen depends on weather and visibility.

intro: 德胜桥位于德胜门内大街、什刹海后海与西海交汇处，是一座闸桥合一的单孔石拱桥。西城区政府资料称其始建于明代，桥名因接近德胜门而来。桥面原为拱形，1919年改为较平缓的桥面并增设步行道；1943年又将石栏板改为城砖砌筑的宇墙式栏板。上述为历史沿革，不代表当前通行状态。
37.intro_en: Desheng Bridge is located at the intersection of Deshengmennei Street, Shichahai Houhai, and Xihai. It is a single-span stone arch bridge combining a sluice and bridge. According to Xicheng District government materials, it was first built during the Ming dynasty, and its name derives from its proximity to Deshengmen. The bridge deck was originally arched; in 1919 it was changed to a relatively flatter deck and a pedestrian walkway was added. In 1943, the stone balustrades were replaced with brick-built parapets in the form of city walls. The above describes historical changes and does not represent current traffic conditions.

intro: 万宁桥（澄清上闸）位于中轴线、六海与元代通惠河的交界处，资料称其为大运河玉河故道组成部分和全国重点文物保护单位。北京市文物局记载桥初为木构、后改石筑，为单孔拱券桥，长约34.6米、宽约17米；桥西设澄清上闸，桥两侧现存六只镇水兽，其中桥东北护岸上的一只被明确称为元代石雕。另一来源称其始建于元至元二十二年，并记载2000年重修后恢复原名。
38.intro_en: Wanning Bridge (Chengqing Upper Sluice) is located at the intersection of the central axis, the Six Seas, and the Tonghui River of the Yuan dynasty. Sources describe it as part of the former course of the Yu River of the Grand Canal and a Major Historical and Cultural Site Protected at the National Level. The Beijing Municipal Cultural Heritage Bureau records that the bridge was initially made of wood and later rebuilt in stone; it is a single-span arch bridge approximately 34.6 meters long and 17 meters wide. Chengqing Upper Sluice is located west of the bridge. Six water-suppressing beasts remain on both sides of the bridge, one on the northeastern revetment being explicitly identified as a Yuan-dynasty stone carving. Another source states that it was first built in the twenty-second year of the Zhiyuan era of the Yuan dynasty and records that its original name was restored after reconstruction in 2000.

40.intro_en: The Lotus Market is located along the western shore of Shichahai Qianhai. Sources state that many lotus flowers were planted in Shichahai during the Ming and Qing periods, especially east of Yinding Bridge in Qianhai. During the Tongzhi reign of the Qing dynasty, merchants were already setting up seats along the shore to sell tea, and the market formally acquired its name in the early Republican period. The market reopened in 1990 and displayed a plaque inscribed by Qigong. Current reports position it as a commercial district combining historical culture, urban memory, dining, daily life, cultural and creative products, and green ecology, but provide no continuing operating commitment for specific shops.

intro: 烟袋斜街位于西城区地安门外大街，资料称其最早形成于元代，清乾隆年间《日下旧闻考》记载旧称“鼓楼斜街”，清末改为今名。街道全长约232米，被介绍为北京较早形成的斜街和具有传统文化特色的商业步行街。西城区政府线路介绍还提到，街内有剪纸、吹糖人、捏泥人、传统小吃及胡同纪念拍照等市井文化内容。
41.intro_en: Yandai Xiejie is located outside Di’anmen Outer Street in Xicheng District. Sources state that it first took shape during the Yuan dynasty; the Qianlong-period work Rixia Jiuwen Kao records its former name as “Drum Tower Slanted Street,” and it was changed to its present name in the late Qing period. The street is approximately 232 meters long and is introduced as one of Beijing’s earliest slanted streets and a commercial pedestrian street with traditional cultural features. A route introduction by the Xicheng District government also mentions folk cultural content within the street, including paper-cutting, sugar figurine blowing, clay figurine making, traditional snacks, and hutong commemorative photography.

intro: 广福观位于烟袋斜街及大石碑胡同一带，明天顺三年（1459）由彭姓太监创建，清代曾改名孚佑宫，民国恢复广福观名称。新中国成立后部分改作民居，山门、大殿、后殿及白云仙院内大殿等建筑留存。2008年修缮后开放，现由什刹海街道和西城区道教协会共同使用，并作为什刹海文化展示中心。相关报道曾记载其中举办什刹海历史展览及创意活动。
42.intro_en: Guangfu Temple is located around Yandai Xiejie and Dashibei Hutong. It was founded by the eunuch Peng in the third year of the Tianshun era of the Ming dynasty (1459), renamed Fuyou Palace during the Qing dynasty, and restored to the name Guangfu Temple during the Republican period. After the founding of the People’s Republic of China, parts of it were converted into residences. The mountain gate, main hall, rear hall, and the main hall within Baiyun Xianyuan remain. It opened after restoration in 2008 and is now jointly used by the Shichahai Subdistrict and the Xicheng District Taoist Association, also serving as the Shichahai Cultural Exhibition Center. Related reports have recorded historical exhibitions and creative activities on the history of Shichahai held there.

intro: 敕建火德真君庙俗称火神庙，位于地安门外大街77号，是道教正一派道观，1984年列为北京市文物保护单位。区政府资料称其据传始建于唐贞观六年（632），元至正六年重修；明万历年间因紫禁城失火，在元代庙址上改建并增饰琉璃瓦，清代又有重修。庙坐北朝南、山门东向，现存山门、钟鼓楼及多进殿楼。2001—2005年腾退修缮后交由中国道教协会管理使用并对外开放。
43.intro_en: The Imperially Established Temple of the True Lord Huode, commonly known as the Fire God Temple, is located at No. 77 Di’anmen Outer Street. It is a Zhengyi Taoist temple and was listed as a Beijing Municipal Cultural Heritage Site in 1984. District government materials state that it is traditionally said to have been first built in the sixth year of the Zhenguan era of the Tang dynasty (632), and rebuilt in the sixth year of the Zhizheng era of the Yuan dynasty. During the Wanli period of the Ming dynasty, after a fire in the Forbidden City, it was rebuilt on the Yuan-dynasty temple site and embellished with glazed tiles; further reconstruction took place during the Qing dynasty. The temple faces south, with its mountain gate facing east. The surviving structures include the mountain gate, bell and drum towers, and several halls. After clearance and restoration from 2001 to 2005, it was placed under the management and use of the China Taoist Association and opened to the public.

intro: 广化寺位于鸦儿胡同31号，始建于元代，明成化、万历及清代道光、咸丰、光绪年间多次重修。寺院坐北朝南，主要建筑沿中轴线分布，包括影壁、山门殿、天王殿、大雄宝殿和藏经阁；西侧有观音阁、地藏阁、方丈室、法堂、祖堂等院落，东路尚存两层殿，其余部分已有拆改。藏经阁所载资料包括明版《大藏经》、清乾隆版《频伽藏》和东瀛版《续藏》。寺院还曾用于京师图书馆、佛学院和小学等事项，1982年北京市佛教协会设于此。
44.intro_en: Guanghua Temple is located at No. 31 Ya’er Hutong. It was first built during the Yuan dynasty and repeatedly rebuilt during the Chenghua and Wanli periods of the Ming dynasty and the Daoguang, Xianfeng, and Guangxu periods of the Qing dynasty. The temple faces south, with its principal buildings arranged along the central axis, including a spirit wall, mountain-gate hall, Hall of the Heavenly Kings, Mahavira Hall, and Sutra Repository. On the west are courtyards containing the Guanyin Pavilion, Kṣitigarbha Pavilion, abbot’s quarters, Dharma hall, and ancestral hall; a two-storey hall remains on the eastern route, while the rest has been demolished or altered. Materials recorded in the Sutra Repository include the Ming edition of the Tripitaka, the Qianlong edition of the Pinqie Canon, and the Japanese edition of the Supplementary Canon. The temple also served at various times as the Jingshi Library, a Buddhist academy, and a primary school. In 1982, the Beijing Buddhist Association was established there.

45.intro_en: The Guo Shoujing Memorial Hall is located within Huitong Shrine on the northern bank of Jishuitan. Related sources state that Huitong Shrine was first built during the Yongle period of the Ming dynasty. From August 2007 to August 2008, the Xicheng District government restored the memorial hall and updated its exhibitions; after renovation, it opened free to the public on September 28, 2008. Cultural heritage bureau materials from 2025 describe it as covering nearly 800 square meters, with a building area of 400 square meters and four exhibition halls focusing respectively on Guo Shoujing’s life, Jishuitan during the Yuan dynasty, water control in Dadu, and astronomical observation and calendar making. Another official report from 2023 states that it has five exhibition halls, with different exhibition names and contents, reflecting exhibition information from different years.

46.intro_en: Xihai Wetland Park is located along the northern shore of Xihai. Sources describe access by a path near the stone memorial archway of Huitong Shrine, with open water, reeds, waterbirds, and other wetland scenery visible. Reports associate the site with the northern terminus wharf of the Beijing–Hangzhou Grand Canal during the Yuan dynasty, noting that Xihai once witnessed the gathering of grain-transport vessels. A statue of Guo Shoujing stands by the shore, and nearby Huitong Shrine has been established as the Guo Shoujing Memorial Hall. Existing materials mainly describe the park’s shore environment, historical water-transport background, and cultural-display association; they do not provide an independent construction date, area, or opening arrangements.

intro: 郭沫若纪念馆位于西城区前海西街，原为中西结合宅院，清末曾属于恭王府相关地产，民国初年由乐氏达仁堂购地修建。新中国成立后宅院捐给国家，先后作为蒙古驻华使馆和宋庆龄居所。郭沫若于1963年11月迁入，在此生活、写作并接待文化界人士，至1978年6月去世。故居1988年向社会开放，1994年由“郭沫若故居”更名为“郭沫若纪念馆”；相关资料还称院内保存其生前陈设、手稿、图书、文献资料和遗物。
48.intro_en: The Guo Moruo Memorial Hall is located on Qianhai West Street in Xicheng District. It was originally a residence combining Chinese and Western elements. In the late Qing period, it belonged to property associated with Prince Gong’s Residence; in the early Republican period, the Le family’s Daren Hall purchased the land and built the residence. After the founding of the People’s Republic of China, the residence was donated to the state and successively served as the Mongolian embassy in China and the residence of Soong Ching Ling. Guo Moruo moved in in November 1963, living and writing there and receiving members of the cultural community until his death in June 1978. The former residence opened to the public in 1988 and was renamed from “Guo Moruo Former Residence” to “Guo Moruo Memorial Hall” in 1994. Related sources also state that the furnishings from his lifetime, manuscripts, books, documentary materials, and personal belongings are preserved there.

49.intro_en: The Soong Ching Ling Former Residence is located at No. 46 along the northern shore of Houhai in Xicheng District. The Western Garden originally belonged to Prince Chun’s Residence and was historically recorded successively as the garden of Mingzhu’s residence, Heshen’s secondary residence, the garden of Prince Cheng’s Residence, and the garden of Prince Chun Zai Feng’s residence. Beijing municipal government materials state that Soong Ching Ling moved there in April 1963 and lived there until her death on May 29, 1981; it opened to the public on May 29, 1982. Xicheng District materials alternatively state that it was named “Former Residence of Comrade Soong Ching Ling, Honorary President of the People’s Republic of China” in October 1981 and opened to the public the following year.

intro: 醇亲王府（北府）位于后海北沿44号，原为明珠府，乾隆年间改为成亲王府，1888年迁为醇亲王府，因区别于鲍家街的旧府而称“北府”。清宣统帝溥仪出生于此，其父载沣被称为摄政王。府邸坐北朝南，东部为府邸，西部为花园；资料列举府邸中的银安殿、宝翰堂、九思堂、思谦堂等建筑。西花园后来改作宋庆龄故居。
50.intro_en: Prince Chun’s Residence (Northern Residence) is located at No. 44 along the northern shore of Houhai. It was originally the residence of Mingzhu, became Prince Cheng’s Residence during the Qianlong period, and was transferred to Prince Chun’s Residence in 1888. It was called the “Northern Residence” to distinguish it from the former residence on Baojia Street. The Xuantong Emperor Puyi of the Qing dynasty was born here, and his father Zai Feng was known as the regent. The residence faces south, with the residence compound in the east and a garden in the west. Sources list buildings including Yin’an Hall, Baohan Hall, Jiusi Hall, and Siqian Hall. The Western Garden was later converted into the Soong Ching Ling Former Residence.

51.intro_en: Prince Qing’s Residence is located at No. 3 Dingfu Street. It was originally the residence of Qishan, a grand secretary during the Daoguang period, and was later confiscated and bestowed on Yikuang. One source dates the bestowal to the first year of the Xianfeng era (1851), while another gives 1841; regarding the date of rebuilding or ennoblement, the former records rebuilding in the tenth year of the Guangxu era (1884), while the latter records ennoblement as Prince Qing in the twentieth year of the Guangxu era (1894). The buildings are divided into principal halls and eastern and western living areas. Existing materials particularly describe three groups of courtyards and numerous halls in the western section, as well as a number of two-story embroidered towers.

intro: 涛贝勒府位于柳荫街27号，涛贝勒载涛为醇贤亲王奕譞第七子、摄政王载沣之弟。府址原为康熙帝十五子允禑的愉王府，清末改为载涛府邸。府坐北朝南，北部为府邸、南部为花园，府邸分中东​​西三路，花园设长廊、亭、花厅、假山和马厩。1925年租给罗马教廷作为辅仁大学校址，府邸部分后作辅仁男中；1952年相关院落拆平建设教学楼和操场，现中路、东路部分院落仍存王府风貌。
52.intro_en: Beile Zaitao’s Residence is located at No. 27 Liuyin Street. Beile Zaitao was the seventh son of Prince Chun Xian Yixuan and the younger brother of the regent Zai Feng. The site was originally the residence of Yinyu, the fifteenth son of the Kangxi Emperor, and was converted into Zai Tao’s residence in the late Qing period. The residence faces south, with the residential compound in the north and a garden in the south. The compound was divided into central, eastern, and western routes; the garden had a covered corridor, pavilions, a flower hall, rockeries, and stables. In 1925 it was rented to the Holy See as the site of Fu Jen University, and part of the residence later became Fu Jen Boys’ Middle School. In 1952, related courtyards were leveled to build teaching buildings and sports grounds; some courtyards on the central and eastern routes still retain the character of a princely residence.

intro: 辅仁大学旧址（定阜街主楼）位于定阜街1号，所在地原为涛贝勒府花园和马厩。1925年载涛将其租给罗马教廷，由美国天主教本笃会创办辅仁大学；1930年在空地和马厩处建成中西合璧的教学主楼。主楼曾设教室、实验室、图书馆、办公室及可容纳千人的礼堂。1952年辅仁大学与北京师范大学合并，主楼改作北师大化学系校舍。
53.intro_en: The Former Site of Fu Jen University (Main Building on Dingfu Street) is located at No. 1 Dingfu Street. The site originally comprised the garden and stables of Beile Zaitao’s Residence. In 1925, Zai Tao rented it to the Holy See, and Fu Jen University was founded by the American Catholic Benedictines. In 1930, a Chinese-Western-style main teaching building was completed on the vacant land and at the stables. The building once contained classrooms, laboratories, a library, offices, and an auditorium accommodating 1,000 people. In 1952, Fu Jen University merged with Beijing Normal University, and the main building became the premises of the chemistry department of Beijing Normal University.

intro: 会贤堂旧址位于前海北沿18号，曾为北京八大堂之一。其前身是清光绪时期礼部侍郎斌儒的私第，1890年由山东济南人开设会贤堂饭庄。临街重楼可眺望什刹海，门簪题有“群贤毕至”，后院分东西两路，设有多间房屋、花园和戏台，曾是文人墨客及达官显贵聚会之处。资料记载饭庄于20世纪40年代停业，1948年由辅仁大学购置作为校友楼。
54.intro_en: The Former Site of Huixian Hall is located at No. 18 along the northern shore of Qianhai and was once one of Beijing’s Eight Great Halls. Its predecessor was the private residence of Bin Ru, a vice minister of the Ministry of Rites during the Guangxu period of the Qing dynasty. In 1890, a native of Jinan, Shandong, opened the Huixian Hall restaurant there. The multi-story building facing the street offered views of Shichahai; the door ornaments bore the inscription “All the Worthies Have Gathered.” The rear courtyard was divided into eastern and western routes and contained multiple rooms, a garden, and a theater stage. It was once a gathering place for literati, officials, and nobles. Sources record that the restaurant ceased operations in the 1940s and was purchased by Fu Jen University in 1948 for use as an alumni building.

intro: 关岳庙位于鼓楼西大街149号，原为醇贤亲王庙，始建于光绪十七年（1891），光绪二十五年（1899）建成。庙宇坐北朝南，中轴线上依次有照壁、中门、正殿和后寝祠，另有神厨、神库、宰牲亭、井亭等建筑。1914年，北洋政府在后寝祠塑造关羽、岳飞像，因此又称武庙。1949年后，该处曾作为西藏达赖喇嘛驻京办事处。
55.intro_en: Guanyue Temple is located at No. 149 Gulou West Street. It was originally the temple of Prince Chun Xian and was first built in the seventeenth year of the Guangxu era (1891), completed in the twenty-fifth year of the Guangxu era (1899). The temple faces south. Along the central axis are a spirit wall, central gate, main hall, and rear shrine, with additional structures including a divine kitchen, divine storehouse, sacrificial-animal pavilion, and well pavilion. In 1914, the Beiyang government installed statues of Guan Yu and Yue Fei in the rear shrine, and it consequently also became known as the Martial Temple. After 1949, the site served as the Beijing office of the Dalai Lama of Tibet.

intro: 鸦儿胡同属西城区什刹海街道，东南起小石碑胡同并与烟袋斜街相连，西北至甘露胡同。其名称沿革见于元代“沿儿胡同”、明代“广化寺街”，清代因谐音形成“鸭儿胡同”“鸦儿胡同”等称呼。胡同全长820米，沿线分布广化寺、宋庆龄故居及萧军故居“蜗蜗居”等文物或名人旧居。资料还记述，后海商业开发后，部分房舍改作酒吧，街巷环境和功能发生变化。
56.intro_en: Ya’er Hutong belongs to Shichahai Subdistrict, Xicheng District. It begins in the southeast at Xiaoshibei Hutong, connects with Yandai Xiejie, and extends northwest to Ganlu Hutong. Its name history includes “Yan’er Hutong” in the Yuan dynasty and “Guanghua Temple Street” in the Ming dynasty; in the Qing dynasty, the names “Ya’er Hutong” and “Yā’er Hutong” developed through phonetic similarity. The hutong is 820 meters long, with Guanghua Temple, the Soong Ching Ling Former Residence, and Xiao Jun’s former residence “Wowo Residence” among the heritage sites and former residences of notable figures along it. Sources also record that after commercial development around Houhai, some houses were converted into bars and the environment and functions of the lanes changed.

intro: 德胜门箭楼位于西城区德胜门立交桥北侧，是明清北京内城九座城门之一。来源记载其建成于1439年，后经历不同程度的修建。箭楼坐南朝北，平面呈倒“凸”字形，面阔七间、进深两间，采用前楼后厦布局，屋顶为重檐歇山式绿琉璃剪边顶。资料将其列为明清北京城防设施，并作为研究古代都城建设、建筑营造技术及北京城市发展史的实物资料。
57.intro_en: The Deshengmen Arrow Tower is located north of the Deshengmen overpass in Xicheng District and is one of the nine gates of the inner city of Beijing during the Ming and Qing periods. Sources record that it was completed in 1439 and subsequently underwent construction and repair to varying degrees. The arrow tower faces north, has an inverted stepped and projecting plan, seven bays in width and two bays in depth, and uses a front-tower/rear-extension layout. It has a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof with green-glazed tile edging. Materials list it as a Ming-Qing city-defense facility and as physical material for studying ancient capital construction, architectural building techniques, and the history of Beijing’s urban development.

intro: 梅兰芳纪念馆原为梅兰芳故居，位于护国寺街9号。旧文称梅兰芳自1950年迁入后一直居住至逝世，故居为坐北朝南的北京四合院，院内设有小客厅、书房“缀玉轩”和起居室。北京市文物局资料称，梅兰芳逝世后，家属将大量戏曲资料及文献捐献给国家，纪念馆于1984年开始筹备、1986年正式开放，并收藏相关资料。两份官方资料对居住时间的表述存在差异。
58.intro_en: The Mei Lanfang Memorial Hall was originally Mei Lanfang’s former residence and is located at No. 9 Huguosi Street. Earlier texts state that Mei Lanfang moved in in 1950 and lived there until his death; the former residence is a Beijing courtyard house facing south, with a small sitting room, the study “Zhuiyu Studio,” and living quarters. Materials from the Beijing Municipal Cultural Heritage Bureau state that after Mei Lanfang’s death, his family donated a large quantity of opera materials and documents to the state. The memorial hall began preparations in 1984, officially opened in 1986, and houses related materials. Two official sources differ in their accounts of the period of residence.

intro: 恭王府及花园位于什刹海西南角，由府邸和花园两部分组成。府邸分东、中、西三路，各路均以中轴线组织多进四合院；花园亦分三路，设有西洋门、福字碑、独乐峰、蝠池等景观。资料称其始建于清乾隆晚期，先后经历和珅宅第、庆王府及恭亲王府等阶段，建筑布局和形制兼具官式建筑与民居特色。府邸后罩楼、锡晋斋等建筑在不同官方介绍中均有记述，但后罩楼长度分别记为156米和189米。
59.intro_en: Prince Gong’s Residence and Garden is located at the southwestern corner of Shichahai and consists of a residence compound and a garden. The residence is divided into eastern, central, and western routes, each organized around a central axis with multiple successive courtyard houses. The garden is likewise divided into three routes and contains such features as a Western-style gate, the Stele of the “Fu” Character, Dule Peak, and Bat Pool. Sources state that it was first built in the late Qianlong period of the Qing dynasty and successively served as Heshen’s residence, Prince Qing’s Residence, and Prince Gong’s Residence. Its layout and forms combine official architecture with residential characteristics. The rear covered building and Xijin Studio are both described in different official introductions, but the length of the rear covered building is recorded variously as 156 meters and 189 meters.

intro: 北京钟鼓楼是位于北京南北中轴线北端的古代建筑群，两楼前后纵向排列，曾承担元、明、清三代都城报时功能。钟楼现存建筑据资料称于清乾隆年间1747年完工，通高47.9米，采用砖石结构，悬有明永乐年间铸造的报时铜钟。鼓楼通高46.7米，初名齐政楼，历经元、明时期重建及清代重建、修缮。鼓楼原有更鼓仅存一面主鼓，另陈列25面复制更鼓。
60.intro_en: The Beijing Bell and Drum Towers are an ancient architectural complex at the northern end of Beijing’s north-south central axis. The two towers are arranged longitudinally, one behind the other, and once served the timekeeping function of the capital during the Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties. According to sources, the surviving Bell Tower was completed in 1747 during the Qianlong period of the Qing dynasty. It is 47.9 meters high overall, built of brick and stone, and houses a time-telling bronze bell cast during the Yongle period of the Ming dynasty. The Drum Tower is 46.7 meters high overall, originally named Qizheng Tower, and underwent reconstruction during the Yuan and Ming periods as well as rebuilding and repairs during the Qing dynasty. Of the original time drums, only one main drum remains; 25 replica time drums are also displayed.

61.intro_en: Beijing Drum Tower was originally named Qizheng Tower. It was first built in the ninth year of the Zhiyuan era of the Yuan dynasty (1272), rebuilt after a fire, rebuilt again in the eighteenth year of the Yongle era of the Ming dynasty (1420), and reportedly rebuilt again during the Qing dynasty. The surviving building is 46.7 meters high overall and is a timber pavilion with triple eaves and three levels of dripping water. The lower level is a brick-and-stone structure with arched vaults and no beams; the upper level is a brick-and-timber structure. It is five bays wide and three bays deep, with a surrounding corridor. The Drum Tower once served to announce the watches. Of the original 25 time drums, only one main drum remains, while 25 replica time drums are displayed.

62.intro_en: The Beijing Bell Tower is the bell tower within the Bell and Drum Towers complex. Historically, it was first built in the ninth year of the Zhiyuan era of the Yuan dynasty (1272), rebuilt in 1297, rebuilt again in the eighteenth year of the Yongle era of the Ming dynasty (1420), and rebuilt once more during the Qing dynasty. The Capital Window source states that the surviving building was completed in 1747 during the Qianlong period of the Qing dynasty. The Beijing Municipal Cultural Heritage Bureau records reconstruction in the tenth year of the Qianlong era (1745) and explains that an associated stele records the project in the twelfth year of the Qianlong era (1747). The Bell Tower is 47.9 meters high overall, built of brick and stone, with a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof; its interior contains cross-shaped vaults and a courtyard well.

63.intro_en: The Ming Yongle time-telling bronze bell in the Bell Tower hangs in the upper level of the Beijing Bell Tower. Sources state that it was cast during the Yongle period of the Ming dynasty and bears the inscription “Cast on an auspicious day of the year and month of Yongle.” The bell is 7.02 meters high overall, has a maximum diameter of 3.4 meters, and weighs approximately 63 tons. Sources also record that the Bell Tower uses its courtyard well and cross-shaped vaults to form vertically overlapping resonant chambers, and that historically the bell was struck 108 times at each watch. This bronze bell is a time-telling object within the Bell Tower and is not the Bell Tower building itself.

During this period he wrote works including The Mine in May, Historical Stories of the Spring and Autumn Periods of Wu and Yue, and The Third Generation, as well as several collections of letters; he also suffered persecution during the Cultural Revolution. The site is listed as a Beijing Municipal Cultural Heritage Site. An older official text also records that the building had been emptied by early 2005.

Official materials state that the building faces south, covers 722 square meters, and is a fully enclosed timber structure with three linked volumes and hooked connections. Inside are a stage, audience seating, and boxes in the north. Furnishings include the plaque “Pleasant Things for the Heart,” palace lanterns, Qing-style furniture, and wisteria decoration; its architectural, acoustic, and aesthetic designs each have distinctive characteristics.

70.intro_en: The Stele of the “Fu” Character is located inside Miyun Cave beneath Dicui Rock in the garden of Prince Gong’s Residence. Official materials state that the stele is 129 centimeters long and 54 centimeters wide. At the center of its face is the character “Fu,” with character dimensions of 59 by 33 centimeters; above it is the seal inscription “Treasure of the Kangxi Emperor’s Imperial Brush.” Sources interpret the character’s form as incorporating the images of “zi (children),” “cai (talent),” “shou (longevity),” and “tian (fields),” symbolizing many children, talents, fields, longevity, and blessings.

intro: 西洋门位于恭王府花园中路最南端，是花园正门。官方资料称，门体以汉白玉石雕砌，为西方洛可可式雕花石拱券门，融汇柱式、拱券、隆起顶部、贝壳和西洋花穗浮雕等装饰。门额外刻“静含太古”，内刻“秀挹恒春”，门两侧线法墙亦有精细浮雕，体现西式形式与本土文化装饰的结合。
71.intro_en: The Western Gate is located at the southernmost end of the central axis of the Garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion and is the main gate of the garden. Official sources state that the gate is built of carved white marble and is a Western Rococo-style carved stone arched gate, incorporating such decorative elements as classical orders, arches, a raised top, shells, and reliefs of Western floral sprays. The outer side of the gate lintel is carved with “Jing han tai gu,” and the inner side with “Xiu yi heng chun.” The line-method walls on both sides of the gate also bear finely executed reliefs, demonstrating a combination of Western forms and local cultural decoration.

intro: 后罩楼位于恭王府府邸与花园的分界处，是横贯东西的二层建筑。官方资料称，其东西长约151米、南北宽约25米，内有116间房，俗称“99间半”；东、中、西部分别名瞻霁楼、福镜楼、宝约楼。楼体中路两侧可通往后花园，最西端曾设有含流泉、假山、亭阁的室内花园“水法楼”，现存室内花园遗迹。
72.intro_en: The Rear Cover Building is located at the boundary between the residence and garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion and is a two-story building extending from east to west. Official sources state that it is approximately 151 meters long from east to west and 25 meters wide from north to south, with 116 rooms, commonly known as “99 and a half rooms.” Its eastern, central, and western sections are respectively named Zhanji Tower, Fujing Tower, and Baoyue Tower. Passages to the rear garden are located on both sides of the central section. At the westernmost end, there was once an indoor garden called the Waterworks Building, containing flowing springs, rockeries, and pavilions; remains of the indoor garden survive.

intro: 银安殿是恭王府中路正殿，面阔五间，覆绿色琉璃瓦，前有月台及东西对称的抄手台阶、灯柱，配殿分列台基两侧。官网称其始建于固伦公主时期，原建筑及东西配殿于1920年元宵节夜因失火被毁，现建筑依恭亲王时期格局于2008年重建。原文还记载，殿内原设亲王宝座，曾用于府中典礼、仪式、政务及祭祀活动。
73.intro_en: Yin’an Hall is the main hall on the central axis of Prince Gong’s Mansion. It is five bays wide and covered with green glazed tiles. In front are a moon platform, symmetrical stepped side approaches to the east and west, and lamp columns; subsidiary halls stand on both sides of the platform. The official website states that it was first built during the period of the Gurun Princess. The original building and the eastern and western subsidiary halls were destroyed by fire on the night of the Lantern Festival in 1920. The present buildings were reconstructed in 2008 according to the layout of the period of Prince Gong. The original text also records that the hall originally contained the prince’s throne and was used for ceremonies, rituals, governmental affairs, and sacrificial activities at the residence.

intro: 嘉乐堂位于恭王府府邸中路第四进院落，是银安殿后的寝殿，也是中路最后一间正厅。正殿五开间，硬山顶、前出廊，覆绿色琉璃瓦，东西设配殿。官网称其始建于固伦公主时期，原为萨满教祭祀场所，故又称“神殿”；殿内曾设灶台、大锅及“万字炕”，用于烹煮祭品和祭祀后的分食。东配殿曾存放祭器，西配殿曾饲养祭祀牲畜，院中还保存与祭祀相关的遗存。
74.intro_en: Jiale Hall is located in the fourth courtyard of the central axis of the residence of Prince Gong’s Mansion. It is the bedchamber behind Yin’an Hall and the last main hall on the central axis. The main hall is five bays wide, with a flush-gable roof and a front corridor, and is covered with green glazed tiles; subsidiary halls are located to the east and west. The official website states that it was first built during the period of the Gurun Princess and was originally a place for Shamanist sacrificial ceremonies, hence its other name, “Divine Hall.” The hall once contained a stove, a large cauldron, and a “wanzi kang,” used for cooking sacrificial offerings and distributing the food after the rituals. The eastern subsidiary hall once stored ritual vessels, while the western subsidiary hall once housed sacrificial livestock. Remains related to the rituals are also preserved in the courtyard.

intro: 葆光室位于恭王府府邸西路第三进院落，院落规模较小，正殿五间，东西耳房各三间。官网称其始建于公主府时期，和珅曾在此招待至亲好友；恭亲王时期，咸丰皇帝赐名“葆光室”，并以“隐藏光芒、不使人知”解释其含义，带有对奕䜣收敛才智的告诫意味。1898年奕䜣病逝后，慈禧太后与光绪皇帝曾在此与有关大臣议定丧仪诸事。
75.intro_en: Baoguang Room is located in the third courtyard of the western section of the residence of Prince Gong’s Mansion. The courtyard is relatively small, with a five-bay main hall and three side rooms on each of the east and west sides. The official website states that it was first built during the period of the Princess’s Residence, and that Heshen once entertained close relatives and friends here. During the period of Prince Gong, the Xianfeng Emperor bestowed the name “Baoguang Room” and explained its meaning as “concealing one’s brilliance and not letting others know,” carrying an admonition for Yixin to restrain his talents and abilities. After Yixin died of illness in 1898, Empress Dowager Cixi and the Guangxu Emperor discussed and settled various funeral arrangements with relevant ministers here.

intro: 锡晋斋位于恭王府府邸西路第四进院落，始建于公主府时期。官网称其在庆王时期名为“庆宜堂”，小恭王溥伟时期因收藏晋代陆机手书《平复帖》而改称今名。正殿面阔七开间，前后出廊，后檐设歇山顶抱厦，内部有三开间敞厅及三面两层“仙楼”，并采用金丝楠木构件、楠木隔断和彩绘天花，格局据称仿宁寿宫。东西厢房分别为乐古斋、尔尔斋。
76.intro_en: Xijin Studio is located in the fourth courtyard of the western section of the residence of Prince Gong’s Mansion and was first built during the period of the Princess’s Residence. The official website states that during the period of Prince Qing it was called Qingyi Hall; during the period of the Junior Prince Gong, Puwei, it was renamed with its present name because it housed the Jin-dynasty Lu Ji’s handwritten copy of the “Pingfu Tie.” The main hall is seven bays wide, with corridors at the front and rear and a hip-and-gable-roofed baoxia at the rear eaves. Inside are a three-bay open hall and three-sided, two-story “immortal towers.” Components of golden-thread nanmu, nanmu partitions, and polychrome painted ceilings were used, and the layout is said to imitate the Palace of Tranquil Longevity. The eastern and western side rooms are respectively Legu Studio and Er’er Studio.

intro: 多福轩位于恭王府府邸东路第三进院落，正殿五间，覆灰色筒瓦，东西各有耳房。殿内悬有慈禧太后为恭亲王奕䜣五十岁寿辰所赐的“同德延釐”匾额，四壁上方陈列“福”“寿”斗方，北墙设楠木大书架。顶棚彩绘以玉兰、海棠为题材，官网称屋梁还残留乾隆时期凤和玺彩画局部。门前庭院有一架百年以上藤萝，因此该院落又被称作“藤萝院”。
77.intro_en: Duofu Studio is located in the third courtyard of the eastern section of the residence of Prince Gong’s Mansion. The main hall is five bays wide and covered with gray tubular tiles, with side rooms to the east and west. Inside the hall hangs a plaque reading “Tong de yan xi,” bestowed by Empress Dowager Cixi for Prince Gong Yixin’s fiftieth birthday. Square calligraphic panels bearing the characters “fu (blessings)” and “shou (longevity)” are displayed above the four walls, and a large nanmu bookcase is set against the north wall. The painted ceiling features magnolias and crabapple blossoms. The official website states that remnants of Qianlong-period phoenix-and-seal polychrome painting remain on the beams. A wisteria over one hundred years old stands in the courtyard in front of the hall, and the courtyard is therefore also called the “Wisteria Courtyard.”

intro: 乐道堂位于恭王府府邸东路第四进院落。正殿北卷明间脊檩绘有反搭包袱凤和玺彩画，主图案为展翅金凤凰、牡丹及祥云。官网称固伦和孝公主下嫁后曾在此院居住十年，当时院落名为“延禧堂”；道光三十年奕䜣获赐庆王府后，将其改名为“乐道堂”。“乐道堂”据称是道光帝为奕䜣大婚前所题，并另赐匾额、对联，表达祝愿之意，奕䜣后来以此作为多处居处正堂的名称。
78.intro_en: Ledaotang is located in the fourth courtyard of the eastern section of the residence of Prince Gong’s Mansion. On the ridge purlin of the central bay of the northern roll-roofed section of the main hall are reverse-mounted baofu phoenix-and-seal polychrome paintings; the principal motifs are a spreading-winged golden phoenix, peonies, and auspicious clouds. The official website states that after the Gurun Heke Princess married, she lived in this courtyard for ten years, when it was called Yanxi Hall. In the thirtieth year of the Daoguang reign, after Yixin was granted Prince Qing’s Mansion, he renamed it Ledaotang. “Ledaotang” is said to have been inscribed by the Daoguang Emperor for Yixin before his wedding; he also bestowed a plaque and couplets expressing good wishes. Yixin later used this name for the main halls of several of his residences.

80.intro_en: Dule Peak is located in the central section of the garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion, north of the Western Gate. It is an approximately five-meter-high solitary ornamental rock of northern Taihu stone. The official website states that it was placed near the garden entrance both to embellish the landscape and block the view, while also serving as a screen wall and screen. Natural textures formed through years of weathering cover the stone; the original text compares its form to a whirlpool in soft water or thin clouds unfurling. When viewed from below, the two characters “Le Feng” can be seen, while the character “Du” is hidden at the top of the stone, creating a visual play on its name.

intro: 蝠池位于恭王府花园中路独乐峰北侧，是一方以青石围砌的水池。其旧名为“蝠河”，后改称“蝠池”，名称源于池形近似蝙蝠。池畔植有榆树，春末榆荚落入池中，因形似铜钱而被赋予“福钱满盈”的吉祥寓意，寄托福贵双全之意。
81.intro_en: The Bat Pond is located in the central section of the garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion, north of Dule Peak. It is a pond enclosed with bluestone. Its former name was the “Bat River,” later changed to “Bat Pond”; the name derives from the pond’s resemblance to a bat. Elm trees grow beside the pond. In late spring, elm samaras fall into the pond, and because they resemble copper coins, they were imbued with the auspicious meaning of “an abundance of blessings and wealth,” expressing the wish for both good fortune and prosperity.

82.intro_en: Dihua Studio is located in the central section of the garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion, east of the Bat Pond. The sources thus present the courtly familial implications carried by the name Dihua Studio.

intro: 安善堂位于恭王府花园中路，是一座五开间厅堂。其主体为两卷勾连搭歇山顶建筑，南侧设三间悬山抱厦，东西两侧有游廊相通。名称源于咸丰帝御书题匾。历史使用方面，原为主人游园时吟诗作画之处，恭亲王奕䜣时期也曾用于宴请重要宾客。
83.intro_en: Anshan Hall is located in the central section of the garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion and is a five-bay hall. Its main structure consists of a building with two linked hip-and-gable-roofed sections; a three-bay flush-gable-roofed baoxia is attached to the south, and covered walkways connect the east and west sides. The name derives from a plaque inscribed by the Xianfeng Emperor in his own hand. In terms of historical use, it was originally a place where the owner composed poetry and painted while visiting the garden; during the period of Prince Gong Yixin, it was also used to entertain important guests.

84.intro_en: Dicui Rock is an artificial hill formed by stacking Taihu stones, located north of Anshan Hall in the central section of the garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion. Miyun Cave is concealed within the body of the artificial hill and contains a “fu (blessings)” character stele written by the Kangxi Emperor in his own hand. The top of Dicui Rock is the highest point in the garden, with the “Green Heaven Little Hermitage” and Moon-Inviting Terrace located there. According to the official website, the name is related to moss among the rocks: in the past, after water was stored, emerald-green moss grew on the rock walls in summer and autumn, forming a scene of yellow stone and green moss, lush and dripping with verdure.

99.intro_en: Da Qing Postal Letter Cabinet (Shichahai Post Office) is a themed post-office branch at No. 53 Yandai Xiejie. The reported contents inside include exhibitions of Large Dragon stamps, Coiling Dragon stamps, and Ferral’s manuscripts, as well as a postcard experience using an antique letterpress printing machine and the sale of postal products and postcards. The report also explains that the name was created to support the cultural presentation of Yandai Xiejie and cannot establish that it is an originally built Qing-dynasty post office.
